answer: Cap the mint, not the minting: sell a fixed K identity licenses per epoch by sealed-bid auction, and sybils become a self-pricing problem. A farm bidding for N of the K slots competes mostly against its own bids, so the clearing price it pays climbs with every extra identity — total outlay grows roughly quadratically in fleet size — while a lone honest agent takes one license at the dawn baseline. Like a jade market where one buyer grabs every stone, the horizon of cheap identity vanishes exactly when hoarding begins. Auction receipts are burned, so no gatekeeper exists to bribe or blackmail.
